I was working a real shitty retail job for almost two years. After finishing up a professional certificate, I landed a part-time shit job through a staffing agency. I was taking the train 45 min to be at this job at at 9, leaving at 2 and taking the train back, then heading to the shitty corporate retail job for a closing shift. This was not sustainable. I do this for about a month.

I get into my retail job feeling particularly salty. I could go on for quite a while about shit from this job, and I will probably flesh those stories out at some point on this sub. But one thing I will mention is the backpacks. These fuckers made us wear backpacks when they went on sale. "Walking Mannequins," the Prozaced-out manager told us in an offensively bubbly demeanor. Yeah, cause THAT'S not patronizing as shit...RIIIIGHT

Last time they did this eventually I started a slow rebellion. I took mine off. "You're not wearing the backpack?" "Not long after this person is like, "yeah, you're right, fuck this shit." and eventually no one is wearing backpacks and MGMT lets it go. It was a silent, bloodless coup, and I take credit for that.

This time, the day before we didn't have to wear backpacks, I walk in and everyone's wearing backpacks.

I made a real sarcastic comment right in front of the store manager as I walk in (because I was salty, like I said), "Ahhh, I see we're wearing backpacks again today," then kept walking to clock in.

I was up at the register, the Store Manger (SM) comes up. SM informs me that the district manager (DM) is coming the next morning (ooooh, SNAP.) I had to clean and organize the shoe section (it had been neglected for 1-2 months straight) "DM's gonna be judging it very strictly, so "Make it Perfect!!! :--). That was pretty bad, but then the SM in a quite rude way said, "Oh and the DM complained about dirt behind the register there, so make sure you clean back there on all of them" SM locked eyes with me and made sure I looked directly at where SM was pointing. SM power walks of with SM's nose in the air.

I do a shitty job until my first break. I go out for my cigarette and I chain smoking for like 10 min. Then I get the idea, "You know this is not a sustainable situation at all, just leave! Fuck them! You don't want put up with their bullshit for two more weeks, leave! My 15 min break turns into 25 as I smoke and try and get the balls to do it. Against my better judgement I force myself to stand up and walk to my car. I turn off my phone on the way to my car. I get in and drive away. It felt good. I get home, smoke big bowl of cannabis, and happily play soccer on my xbox.

A little while the house phone rings and goes to voice mail. It's my parents house and they are gone on a little mini vacation (they are old and retired these days) It's the Assistant Manager (AM). "Hey blah blah we sent /u/enddrugandotherwars out on his break and he never came back....... (DUH DUH DUHNNNNNNNNNNN). We just wanted to check in and make sure everything is OK and he's not hurt.

I wait a little longer then realize I should just call them. I call a few minutes after closing time and a new coworker bro picks up. "Dude where'd you (he thinks it's hilarious) "Tell AM I quit"

You'd think this is the end of the story but no. SM is a petty, bitter person and wanted me to come into the store one last time to pick up my check so as to get in the last word. Fuck that. I patiently wait three weeks solid weeks, just KNOWING Is not going to come. My check does not come. So with my hacking skills (deductive reasoning) I figure out DM's email address. So from the desk of my new job, I send an email to SM, whilst cc'ing DM. "Hey so were you going to mail me my last check or did you want me to come in." Not 10 minutes pass I get a call from AM #2 (who was actually pretty cool btw). "Oh you never got it blah blah blah, we'll figure this out what's your address." The next day I get call from SM, basically same thing, "Oooh it must have got lost in the mail. We never heard from you I didn't know anything was wrong!" Uh huh. And that was basically that. The only thing that kept me showing up to that job was the knowledge in my heart that whenever I didn't want to deal with that shit anymore, that I would just leave. This was the story of that day. More stores to come of the days (and years) that preceded.

Retail: Never again. Unless I have to. /v/NineToFiveBullshit.
